memory_update.text: nVent Electric should remain in the Layer 1 universe for liquid_cooling_and_rack_power because its AI data-center product set spans liquid cooling, racks, power distribution, CDUs, manifolds, and connection systems.

Modine Manufacturing should remain in the Layer 1 universe as an underfollowed thermal-management candidate because recent evidence links data-center growth to AI-related air and liquid cooling projects and tailored CDU offerings.

Powell Industries was not included in the final 3-candidate list due to the limit, but should be tracked in the next pass for electrical distribution equipment, switchgear, and large data-center order exposure.

Need a follow-up pass specifically for sub-$10B and $300M-$1B suppliers in pumps, valves, leak detection, sensors, busway, PDUs, cold plates, and thermal fluids; this pass skewed toward larger public companies with clearer evidence.
The node appears to split into at least three evidence lanes: liquid cooling and CDUs, rack/power distribution and enclosures, and facility-level electrical distribution equipment.

node: Liquid cooling, rack power distribution, thermal controls, and data-center physical infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expanded the direct public-company universe for AI data-center liquid cooling, rack power, and physical infrastructure. The reference lane remains anchored by large, obvious infrastructure vendors such as Vertiv, while the discovery lane points to companies whose AI exposure is embedded in electrical enclosures, coolant distribution units, racks, thermal systems, and modular data-center cooling rather than cleanly labeled as AI semiconductors. This pass is research-only and does not provide trading recommendations.
